skill.name: super-swarm-spark
skill.description: Orchestrates execution of markdown development plans with a rolling pool of Sparky subagents.
skill.summary: Runs plan tasks in parallel while enforcing canonical paths, validation, and integration checks.
skill.author: am-will

security_audit.summary: The static shell-execution findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code and fenced examples. Semantic review found operational risks from forced high-concurrency subagent scheduling, dependency-map bypass, and automatic commits, but no evidence of data exfiltration, credential access, or prompt injection aimed at the reviewer.

remediation.issue: The workflow requires up to 12 concurrent subagents and tells the orchestrator to ignore dependency maps.
remediation.suggestion: Respect dependency metadata by default and allow users to set a lower concurrency limit before execution begins.

remediation.issue: Subagent prompts require each worker to commit its changes.
remediation.suggestion: Make commits optional and require user confirmation before staging or committing any files.

remediation.issue: The skill forces a specific agent role for all launched tasks.
remediation.suggestion: Treat the role as a preference and allow the host agent to choose an available, policy-compliant worker type.

semantic_findings.title: High-Concurrency Agent Orchestration With Dependency Bypass
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells the agent to ignore dependency maps and keep up to 12 subagents running. This can cause conflicting edits, excessive resource use, or unsafe sequencing in development repositories.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions explicitly require high parallelism and say to ignore dependency maps. The risk is operational rather than malicious, but the behavior is clear.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Commit Instruction For Subagents
semantic_findings.description: The task template instructs each subagent to commit work after editing. Automatic commits can make unreviewed changes harder to audit and may interfere with user-controlled version history.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file directly instructs subagents to update the plan and commit their work. It also says never to push, which reduces but does not remove the version-control risk.

content.value_statement: Large development plans often stall when tasks wait for manual coordination. This skill parses plan files, assigns task-specific context, and manages a rolling pool of Sparky subagents.
actual_capabilities: Parses markdown plan files for task sections and optional task subsets.
Builds per-task context packs with canonical files, folders, and naming rules.
Schedules a rolling pool of up to 12 Sparky subagents.
Validates each completed task against expected outcomes before launching more work.
Runs a final integration pass to resolve conflicts, adjust tests, and verify results.
Produces an execution summary with completed tasks, issues, validation, and modified files.
limitations: Requires a clear markdown plan with identifiable task sections.
Assumes a Sparky subagent role is available in the host environment.
High parallelism can create edit conflicts in shared files.
Does not replace human review for commits, test failures, or integration decisions.

use_cases.title: Implement a Multi-Part Feature Plan
use_cases.description: Run several independent feature tasks from one plan while keeping file names and validation steps consistent.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Refactor Work Across Files
use_cases.description: Assign focused refactor tasks to subagents and reconcile shared file changes during the final integration pass.

use_cases.title: Track Execution Status For Planned Work
use_cases.description: Keep the plan file updated with completed tasks, work logs, issues, and validation outcomes.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Full Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use super-swarm-spark to implement every task in ./plans/feature-plan.md. Keep the plan file updated after each completed task.

prompt_templates.title: Run Selected Tasks
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for a subset of planned work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use super-swarm-spark on ./plans/auth-plan.md and run only tasks T1, T2, and T4. Preserve the canonical paths listed in the plan.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Shared File Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use super-swarm-spark for ./plans/refactor-plan.md. Pay special attention to shared-touch files and reconcile conflicts during integration.

prompt_templates.title: Execute With Validation Focus
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request that emphasizes test coverage and final verification.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use super-swarm-spark for ./plans/release-plan.md. Run feasible validation for each task, add missing tests, and report any blocked checks with evidence.

output_examples.output: The agent runs tasks T3 and T7, records completed work in the plan, lists modified files, and reports validation results.
The agent schedules the full plan, validates each task result, resolves integration issues, and returns a concise execution summary.
The agent focuses on task T2, applies the specified file constraints, updates the plan log, and describes any deferred checks.

best_practices: Use plan files with explicit task IDs, canonical paths, acceptance criteria, and validation steps.
Review shared-touch files before running high-concurrency work on large branches.
Inspect the final execution summary and commits before merging any generated changes.
anti_patterns: Do not use vague plans that omit target files, test expectations, or task boundaries.
Do not run high-concurrency tasks on fragile branches without backups or review gates.
Do not treat automatic task completion as a substitute for human code review.

faq.question: What kind of plan file does this skill expect?
faq.answer: It expects a markdown file with task sections, task IDs, locations, acceptance criteria, and validation notes.

faq.question: Can I run only part of a plan?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide task IDs or a task subset so the workflow filters the plan before launching work.

faq.question: How many agents can it run at once?
faq.answer: The skill schedules a rolling pool with up to 12 active Sparky subagents.

faq.question: Does it handle conflicts between parallel tasks?
faq.answer: It instructs the orchestrator to validate completed tasks and perform a final integration pass for conflicts.

faq.question: Does it run tests?
faq.answer: It asks agents to run feasible validation and asks the orchestrator to run required tests during integration.

faq.question: Is it safe to let it commit changes automatically?
faq.answer: Use caution. Review generated changes and consider requiring confirmation before any commit is created.
